title: Order alerts and live ETA
idea: Notifications in a food delivery system are observers of the order's state machine, and the ETA is a phase-aware estimate built from a swappable travel strategy.
points: `Order` publishes one `OrderEvent` per real transition; it never knows channels exist.
Each audience gets its own listener that picks states worth a message.
ETA depends on the phase: while food cooks, the rider rides in parallel.
A `TravelModel` strategy hides speed; rain becomes a wrapper, not an `if`.

hero.title: One order, two audiences, one ETA

messages.label: PLACED → ACCEPTED
messages.note: The kitchen accepts. `Order` builds one `OrderEvent` and hands it to every listener in turn.

messages.label: minutes(ACCEPTED, leg)
messages.note: The customer message needs a time. The calculator takes the longer of prep and rider pickup, then adds the drop.

messages.label: push: cooking
messages.note: `CustomerAlerts` chose the message; the injected `Channel` decides how it travels.

messages.label: ACCEPTED → READY
messages.note: Food is packed. Only `RiderAlerts` cares about this state; the customer listener stays quiet.

messages.label: sms: ready for pickup
messages.note: The rider gets an SMS. A new audience means a new listener, not an edit to `Order`.

messages.label: READY → PICKED_UP
messages.note: The rider has the bag. Prep time no longer matters to the estimate.

messages.label: minutes(PICKED_UP, leg)
messages.note: Only the drop leg is left, so the ETA shrinks to the travel time to the customer.

messages.label: ETA moved ≥ 3 min: send
messages.note: `EtaWatcher` drops a new ETA within 3 minutes of the last one sent. This drop is far larger, so it goes out.

code.title: Alerts as observers
code.caption: The order publishes events; per-audience listeners choose the text and the channel.

walk.text: Wiring happens outside `Order`. A failing listener goes first, so later listeners show they still run.
States from the lifecycle page, an immutable event record, and two one-method contracts.
A repeated state is ignored, so a retried call cannot send a duplicate message.
Each listener runs in its own `try`; the analytics failure is reported, then the customer still gets "delivered".
A `switch` maps states to customer text. Unlisted states return `null` and send nothing.
The rider cares about one state only. Same event, different audience, separate class.

code.title: Phase-aware ETA
code.caption: The ETA formula changes with the order state; travel speed is a strategy; a watcher throttles updates. In a full system `CustomerAlerts` would call the calculator; here they are shown apart.

walk.text: A `Leg` holds what the estimate needs. The compact constructor rejects negative inputs early.
`TravelModel` is the strategy. `Slowdown` wraps any model, so rain needs no new branch.
While cooking, the rider rides to the restaurant in parallel: take the longer, then add the drop.
Later phases drop the parts already done. A `switch` expression must cover every state.
Round up. A customer forgives early food, not a late promise.
`EtaWatcher` sends a new ETA only when it moved by the threshold since the last one sent.

pitfalls: Calling SMS and push inside `moveTo` ties order logic to every channel; publish an event instead.
One listener throwing stops the rest of the loop unless each call is isolated.
Adding prep time and pickup travel overstates ETA; the rider rides while the kitchen cooks.

quiz.q: Same classes as `EtaDemo`. What does this print?
quiz.why: At 30 km/h, 2 km takes 4 minutes and 5 km takes 10. The rider waits for the 15-minute prep: max(15, 4) + 10 = 25.

takeaway: Orders publish events; listeners pick the words; strategies estimate the time.

starters: Should notifications be sent synchronously inside the state change or through a queue?
How would I add a restaurant tablet alert without touching the Order class?
How do real apps refine the ETA once live rider GPS updates arrive?
